authorityBoundary: This graph compares documented game abstractions. It does not authorize a KORAIL procedure, armed station staff, firefighter duties, calibrated hazard physics, or implementation.

scope.targetExperience: Single-player first-person Busan Station and KTX mission experience with the player as KORAIL station staff performing report, broadcast/communication, passenger guidance, evacuation support, access control and site coordination.
scope.learningConstraint: Procedure recall should arise through action, consequence, NPC response and in-world correction. No separate quiz or debrief feature is proposed here.

method.causalityRule: A title, trailer description or marketing adjective does not establish an input-to-feedback mechanic. Concrete claims require a table, named section, patch-note paragraph, developer passage, or inspected footage timestamp.
method.playableEvidenceRule: All six entries are documentation-level benchmarks. No claim says this lane personally reproduced behavior in a current build.

games.title: PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS
games.whySelected: Explicit user reference and a strong example of turning a large uncertain space into embodied movement, route choice, spatial communication and escalating time pressure.

documentedAbstractions.abstraction: a compact stance and speed vocabulary: walk, sprint, crouch, prone, jump/vault and lean

documentedAbstractions.concept: communicating a place faster than describing it
documentedAbstractions.abstraction: point crosshair and place a world/map ping visible to teammates
a shrinking boundary that continuously costs health if ignored

stationStaffSafeTransfer: Use walking pace, brisk movement and collision-aware traversal to make distance and route choice felt.
Let a player point to a world location and convert it into a provisional report or colleague assignment that must be acknowledged.
Represent an authored operational window through changing route availability and visible NPC consequences only when the governing scenario source supports it.
combatOnlyReject: weapon handling, looting and armor economy
last-survivor incentives
health-draining circles as a smoke or evacuation model
free-climbing or vaulting that bypasses station access controls

games.title: Sudden Attack
games.whySelected: Explicit user reference and a useful case of high-tempo attention management through radar, timer, mission-state, radio, sound focus and redundant feedback.

documentedAbstractions.concept: selective attention to sound and urgent events
documentedAbstractions.abstraction: radio shortcuts, footstep volume controls and visual warnings for nearby danger

stationStaffSafeTransfer: Keep the mission HUD compact: current task, known people state and a timer only when source-authorized.
Pair radio, PA, alarm and passenger calls with Korean text and a restrained direction cue.
Make acknowledgements visible in both animation and text so the player knows which instruction an NPC heard.
combatOnlyReject: hit markers, damage numbers and enemy HP
enemy-reveal radar
kill/death scoreboards and streak effects
paid character advantages as training mechanics
games.playableEvidenceScope: Current official Korean guide sections inspected; no local play or latency/legibility test.

documentedAbstractions.abstraction: research and disposable blockouts followed by navigation, door, AI, cover, interactable and sightline passes

Make alternate-route value visible through who can see the guide, which threshold is blocked and where a colleague is stationed.

migrationMatrix.realConcept: A staff member must move through a bounded facility while keeping orientation and deciding when speed is justified.
migrationMatrix.gameAbstraction: A small movement vocabulary makes pace and body position legible without simulating every gait.
migrationMatrix.input: WASD movement; Shift for brief brisk movement; mouse look. Crouch/vault only if a sourced mission and geometry need them.
migrationMatrix.constraint: Collision, stairs, doors, people and access boundaries; no parkour or unrestricted vaulting.
migrationMatrix.observableFeedback: Camera/body acceleration, footstep cadence, NPC yielding/obstruction and route-progress cues.
migrationMatrix.success: Player reaches a supported interaction or guidance position without clipping, teleporting or bypassing an access boundary.
migrationMatrix.failure: Blocked path, loss of line of sight to the group or attempted traversal of an unauthorized boundary.
migrationMatrix.recovery: Slow down, reposition, take the alternate supported path or ask an NPC to clear/hold a threshold.

migrationMatrix.realConcept: A person reporting an incident must identify a location and ensure the receiver understood it.
migrationMatrix.gameAbstraction: Point at a visible site, attach a concise location fact, and require an acknowledgement before the assignment changes state.
migrationMatrix.input: Aim/gaze at a valid world anchor; press context/report; choose one short fact if needed; confirm or cancel.
migrationMatrix.constraint: Line of sight, bounded range, named supported anchors and no through-wall marking. The player cannot report unobserved hidden state.
migrationMatrix.observableFeedback: World marker, Korean phrase echo, radio voice/text acknowledgement and colleague head-turn/movement.
migrationMatrix.success: Acknowledgement repeats the intended location and the receiving NPC acts on that same anchor.
migrationMatrix.failure: Ambiguous anchor, missing required fact, receiver unavailable or contradictory later observation.
migrationMatrix.recovery: Re-point, correct the fact, choose a nearby valid anchor or contact an available colleague.

migrationMatrix.realConcept: Some routes or tasks become less viable as an incident evolves.
migrationMatrix.gameAbstraction: Time is embodied as a changing spatial option and visible mission-state, rather than only a countdown.
migrationMatrix.input: Player observes world cues, checks the compact mission state and chooses a route or task order.
migrationMatrix.constraint: Only authored, source-backed phase changes; no claim that the timing predicts real smoke, crowd or injury dynamics.
migrationMatrix.observableFeedback: Door/route state, PA/radio updates, passenger movement and a timer only when the source defines a real deadline.
migrationMatrix.success: Player changes plan before a declared route or task window closes and guides affected NPCs to the supported alternative.
migrationMatrix.failure: The chosen option becomes unavailable, leaving a recoverable alternate rather than applying unexplained damage.
migrationMatrix.recovery: Receive the update, identify the alternate route, redirect passengers and update the colleague assignment.

migrationMatrix.realConcept: The player must maintain spatial, temporal and communication awareness without stopping movement.
migrationMatrix.gameAbstraction: Stable HUD regions show current task, known people state and source-authorized time; audio cues receive text and direction redundancy.
migrationMatrix.input: Glance-level HUD reading; optional map key; separate audio/subtitle/display settings.
migrationMatrix.constraint: No enemy radar, no omniscient passenger markers, no color-only meaning and no full-screen radio menu during urgent traversal.
migrationMatrix.observableFeedback: Known-state icons, concise Korean text, alarm/radio subtitles and a low-clutter direction cue.
migrationMatrix.success: A player can identify the next action and the source of a cue while continuing to move.
migrationMatrix.failure: Cue is missed, duplicated, ambiguous or exposes information the player never obtained.
migrationMatrix.recovery: Repeat critical radio information, preserve it in a log, allow volume/text scaling and let the player request clarification.

migrationMatrix.realConcept: A guide can influence only people who can see, hear and physically follow them through usable thresholds.
migrationMatrix.gameAbstraction: Doors, corners, corridor width and visible alternatives create route decisions and determine which NPCs receive guidance.
migrationMatrix.input: Look, move, open an allowed threshold, point or issue a guidance cue, then check the group physically.
migrationMatrix.constraint: Routes must be collision- and NPC-navigation tested; no tactical clearing, breaching or source-unsupported interior link.
migrationMatrix.observableFeedback: Line-of-sight highlight at close range, passenger head/voice acknowledgement, actual pathing and lagging/separated state.
migrationMatrix.success: The same passengers traverse the selected continuous route and remain observable or accounted for.
migrationMatrix.failure: A passenger cannot see/hear, a threshold is blocked or the route is too narrow for the authored group.
migrationMatrix.recovery: Return, regroup, reposition the guide, open a permitted alternative or assign a colleague to the threshold.

migrationMatrix.realConcept: People may misunderstand, hesitate, separate, follow others or try to return; an instruction is not the same as compliance.
migrationMatrix.gameAbstraction: Each passenger enters an observable response state based on hearing, visibility, mobility and the current route.
migrationMatrix.input: Address individual/group; point to route; repeat or simplify; call a colleague for support.
migrationMatrix.constraint: No coercion, restraint, morale damage or hidden dice-only refusal. Variation must have a readable cause and bounded recovery.
migrationMatrix.observableFeedback: Spoken response, posture, gaze, movement start, hesitation, separation or a question asking for clarification.
migrationMatrix.success: Passenger begins the intended safe movement or explicitly transfers to another staff member's care.
migrationMatrix.failure: Passenger does not hear, cannot move, follows the wrong group or attempts re-entry.
migrationMatrix.recovery: Re-address, reduce distance, clarify direction, remove the local obstacle or involve the scripted colleague.

migrationMatrix.realConcept: At incident onset, staff possess observations and reports rather than complete ground truth.
migrationMatrix.gameAbstraction: Unknown facts remain hidden; sound, sight and radio reports reveal bounded evidence that can conflict or become stale.
migrationMatrix.input: Look/listen, move to a supported observation point, question an NPC or request a radio repeat.
migrationMatrix.constraint: No invisible adaptive adversary, no fake randomness and no requirement to approach a hazard to fill an information bar.
migrationMatrix.observableFeedback: Directional sound, visible world state, timestamped report text and confidence expressed as source identity rather than a fabricated probability.
migrationMatrix.success: Player bases the next instruction on a confirmed observation or clearly attributed report.
migrationMatrix.failure: Player treats an unconfirmed report as certain or ignores a contradictory observation.
migrationMatrix.recovery: Verify from a safe point, ask for clarification, update the shared fact and redirect affected NPCs.

migrationMatrix.realConcept: A staff action is often mediated by a particular handset, console, barrier or assistance point.
migrationMatrix.gameAbstraction: The world object exposes one dominant contextual verb and visibly changes state when operated.
migrationMatrix.input: Aim within forgiving bounds; press/tap interaction; use short directional or choice input; cancel at any time.
migrationMatrix.constraint: No pixel hunt, precision gesture or physics puzzle. The exact tool, permission and sequence require a KORAIL source.
migrationMatrix.observableFeedback: Target outline/prompt, hand or object animation, progress, sound, Korean status text and changed world/NPC behavior.
migrationMatrix.success: The intended object changes to an acknowledged operational state and downstream actors respond.
migrationMatrix.failure: Wrong object, unavailable permission, missing prerequisite or interrupted action.
migrationMatrix.recovery: Explain the missing prerequisite in-world, release/cancel safely, choose the correct object or ask the authorized NPC.

migrationMatrix.realConcept: Coordination requires assigning a bounded task and knowing whether the colleague accepted, reached and completed it.
migrationMatrix.gameAbstraction: A command becomes an NPC state chain: heard, accepted, moving, working, complete or blocked.
migrationMatrix.input: Select a visible/contactable colleague; point to a supported location; choose one role-valid task; confirm.
migrationMatrix.constraint: Colleague capability, current assignment, path and authority; no firefighter or police task transfer.
migrationMatrix.observableFeedback: Voice/text repeat-back, visible travel, work animation, maintained position and completion/blocked report.
migrationMatrix.success: The colleague physically reaches the location and performs the assigned station-staff action.
migrationMatrix.failure: Task conflicts, no path, colleague unavailable or target invalid.
migrationMatrix.recovery: Reassign, clear the route, choose another colleague or perform the role-valid task directly.

migrationMatrix.realConcept: A response option may require an available person, working device, route, key or other authorized resource.
migrationMatrix.gameAbstraction: The action is gated by a small explicit dependency chain, and the missing link is shown in the world.
migrationMatrix.input: Inspect the target; attempt action; retrieve/request the valid resource; retry or choose an alternate.
migrationMatrix.constraint: Only real, source-backed dependencies. No invented equipment scarcity or inventory grind.
migrationMatrix.observableFeedback: Object state, staff availability, route state and a short explanation of the missing dependency.
migrationMatrix.success: The correct authorized resource enables the action and produces its expected world consequence.
migrationMatrix.failure: Resource absent, busy, inoperable or used at an invalid target.
migrationMatrix.recovery: Request replacement/support, reroute, use another valid method or escalate through the sourced chain.

commonPatterns.pattern: Reality becomes playable when it is reduced to a few situated verbs, explicit constraints and immediate world consequences.
commonPatterns.implication: Start with report, point, guide, assign, operate and account; do not start with a catalogue of real equipment animations.

commonPatterns.pattern: Urgency works when elapsed time changes space, people or available options, not when a timer exists by itself.
commonPatterns.implication: A source-authorized deadline should visibly change route or NPC state and still provide a plausible recovery path.

commonPatterns.pattern: Information is valuable when it is partial, attributed and actionable.
commonPatterns.implication: Distinguish observed, reported, acknowledged and unknown state; avoid omniscient overlays.

commonPatterns.pattern: NPC cooperation is believable when acknowledgement, travel, work and obstruction are visible.
commonPatterns.implication: Never let a command button silently flip a mission flag or teleport a colleague.

commonPatterns.pattern: Route choice is created by visibility, width, thresholds, people and changing availability rather than by decorative map complexity.
commonPatterns.implication: Validate continuous player/NPC routes and sightlines before visual polish.

commonPatterns.pattern: Failure teaches through a readable cause and an in-world correction loop.
commonPatterns.implication: Prefer clarification, regrouping, rerouting and reassignment over instant mission failure or a later quiz.

accessibilityAndAgency.insight: Critical cues need at least two channels.
accessibilityAndAgency.proposal: Pair radio/PA/alarm audio with Korean subtitles and restrained direction or source labels; never encode mission state only by color.

accessibilityAndAgency.insight: Input choice should preserve the decision rather than change the training content.
accessibilityAndAgency.proposal: Remap movement and interaction, expose sensitivity and text/audio scale, and offer tap/hold alternatives for noncontinuous actions.

accessibilityAndAgency.insight: Station-staff competence is attention and judgement, not twitch aim.
accessibilityAndAgency.proposal: Use forgiving interaction cones, named anchors and clarification; do not grade pixel-perfect pointing or reaction speed unless a source explicitly makes time critical.

accessibilityAndAgency.insight: Agency requires visible downstream effects and the ability to revise a decision.
accessibilityAndAgency.proposal: Every report, route choice and colleague assignment should show who heard it, what changed and how the player can correct it.

accessibilityAndAgency.insight: Partial information should constrain knowledge, not remove control.
accessibilityAndAgency.proposal: Withhold unobserved facts but always expose a safe verification path, attributed report or explicit unknown state.

accessibilityAndAgency.insight: Menus should not suspend embodied responsibilities by accident.
accessibilityAndAgency.proposal: Keep radio choices short and contextual; preserve situational audio and allow cancel/retry without losing movement context.

antiPatterns.wrongLesson: Replace a rifle with an extinguisher or radio, keep crosshair, hit points and DPS, and call it procedural training.
antiPatterns.whyWrong: It rewards aim and depletion rather than observation, authority, communication and consequence; it can also imply suppression duties the station-staff role does not have.

antiPatterns.wrongLesson: Show every passenger, hazard and colleague through walls from mission start.
antiPatterns.whyWrong: It removes reporting, accounting, uncertainty and line-of-sight work, and teaches confidence in information the player never obtained.

antiPatterns.wrongLesson: Copy PUBG's shrinking ring or health drain and label it smoke spread, safe distance or evacuation timing.
antiPatterns.whyWrong: The game abstraction has no authority for fire/smoke dynamics and would teach false thresholds.

antiPatterns.wrongLesson: Give station staff suspect pursuit, weapon handling, coercive compliance, breaching or room-clearing procedures because the camera is first person.
antiPatterns.whyWrong: It changes the player role, creates unsafe procedural confusion and imports a police combat problem the user explicitly excluded.

antiPatterns.wrongLesson: A menu click, invisible NPC teleport or later quiz stands in for whether a person heard, moved, was accounted for or reached a supported location.
antiPatterns.whyWrong: It separates recall from action and conceals causal failure; the latest product direction requires learning through play.

questions: Does any proposed transfer accidentally give station staff police, firefighter or armed-counterterror authority?
Does each urgency mechanic alter an observable option without pretending to model real smoke, injury or safe distance?
Does every NPC failure have a visible cause and an in-world recovery instead of hidden randomness?
Does the HUD expose only observed, reported or acknowledged information?
Can the same procedural judgement be exercised with remapped input, subtitles and lower pointer precision?
Are report, broadcast, guidance, evacuation support, access control and site coordination still the dominant verbs?
jevReviewPacket.minimumPass: No role violation; no unsupported hazard claim; no omniscient state; every failure recoverable or explicitly technical; every accepted mission mechanic bound to a public KORAIL/manual/drill source before implementation.

nextUse: Root joins T02-T10 to verified KORAIL manual/drill facts. A pattern with no procedural source remains a design candidate, not a mission requirement.
Jev reviews role and causality boundaries before root proposes missions to the user.
Only after user selects a proposal should implementation bind inputs, NPC states, equipment and routes in Unity.
The existing unpublished controller draft remains generic and unvalidated; this research does not approve publication.

validation.writeBoundary: Only requested research/planning paths were changed by this lane.
limitations: No videos were used as causal proof solely from their title or description.
The GDC Alien overview supports only its stated design goals, not detailed AI architecture.
Ready or Not Vol.90 described a then-upcoming feature and is retained as developer design evidence, not current-build verification.
Official product pages may describe intended or marketed behavior; hands-on reliability remains untested.
No claim is made about proprietary code, physical accuracy or state-of-the-art AI.
